comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official prospective-student pages establish a coherent 180-EC Artificial Intelligence curriculum: a fixed 60-EC first year; 48 EC of compulsory second-year study plus 12 EC of restricted electives; and a third year comprising 24 EC of restricted electives, 24 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The pages identify the overview as provisional for 2026-2027. Because the programme has elective baskets rather than formal named routes, the comparator instantiates exactly the required credits using the first listed options in official source order: Bayesian Networks, Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Cognitive Science in year 2; and the first five year-3 options, totalling 24 EC. This neutral tie-break is independent of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Artificial intelligence, cognition & intelligent systems
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Artificial Intelligence programme combining programming, mathematical reasoning, data, machine learning, deep learning, robotics, planning and algorithms with cognition, neuroscience, perception, language, ethics, experimental methods and human-centred communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates computational AI with substantial cognitive-science and intelligent-systems study, so the label names all three organising elements.
progression: Programming, mathematics, data, brain-and-behaviour and research foundations precede advanced algorithms, optimisation, deep learning, robotics, cognition and psycholinguistics. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Computational AI & autonomous systems
alternatives.concept: A computational AI route centred on programming, algorithms, software, mathematical and statistical modelling, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimisation, robotics, computer vision, databases, networks and autonomous agents.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum's dense programming, algorithms, mathematics, learning, optimisation and robotics sequence supports a computational and autonomous-systems label.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the cognitive route, this curriculum replaces much of the psychology, neuroscience and philosophy content with databases, networks, software development, advanced algorithms, reinforcement learning and numerical methods.
progression: Research, mathematics, data and database foundations precede programming-intensive software, robotics, algorithms, optimisation, reinforcement learning and deep learning. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede every course that formally requires them, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Cognitive AI, language & neuroscience
alternatives.concept: A cognitive AI route centred on computational models of mind, brain and behaviour, combining cognition, neuroscience, perception, language, psychology and philosophy with programming, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, logic, mathematics and experimental research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines AI methods with a sustained sequence in cognitive science, neuroscience, psychology, language and philosophy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and computational alternatives, this route gives substantially greater weight to neurobiology, lifespan and social psychology, perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, philosophy of mind, agency and advanced behavioural research.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, neurobiology, mathematics, programming and statistical foundations precede perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, deep learning, computer vision, algorithms and advanced research. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two generator-backed and feasible organising directions: computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems; and cognitive AI, language and neuroscience. Each produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached. Application-sector outcomes such as healthcare, transport, finance and education support these directions but do not independently generate additional alternatives.

blocks: Both provide introductory programming and computational problem-solving foundations.
Both develop programming beyond the introductory level; UCR emphasises software engineering and multiple paradigms.
Both extend computational reasoning beyond introductory programming; the UCR course emphasises advanced algorithms rather than programming-language concepts.
Both address symbolic or knowledge-based intelligent behaviour, planning and reasoning under constraints.
UCR builds AI across several courses but has no single scheduled survey identical to this introductory component.
UCR courses address intelligent systems and social application, but no single course reproduces this restricted elective.
Both develop predictive modelling from data; UCR surveys major machine-learning methods.
Both provide substantial neural-network and deep-learning theory and implementation.
Both directly develop reinforcement-learning theory and algorithms.
Both provide dedicated robotics study; UCR emphasises kinematics, manipulation and motion planning.
Both provide foundational calculus and mathematical methods for later modelling.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations through matrices, vectors and transformations.
Both develop formal reasoning, logic and discrete structures for AI.
Both introduce probability foundations; UCR combines probability with statistical inference.
Both develop statistical modelling and analysis; UCR focuses on multivariate and experimental human-data methods.
Both extend mathematical problem solving; UCR emphasises numerical algorithms rather than a second calculus sequence.
Both provide research design, experiments, sampling and introductory statistical methodology.
UCR offers image processing, computer vision and linear algebra, but no single scheduled course reproduces a dedicated digital-signal-processing component.
UCR Probability & Statistics covers inference and probability, but not a dedicated six-credit Bayesian-statistics sequence.
UCR AI and probability courses provide related tools but no single dedicated Bayesian-networks course.
Both provide broad psychological and cognitive foundations; UCR integrates these with neuroscience and behaviour.
Both provide biological foundations for understanding the brain.
Both examine cognition through interdisciplinary scientific perspectives; UCR focuses on higher-order cognitive functions.
Both investigate language; UCR focuses on human language processing rather than computational NLP.
UCR combines neurobiology, cognition and computation across courses but has no single dedicated computational-neuroscience component.
UCR offers neuroscience, perception and computing courses but no dedicated brain-computer-interface course.
UCR supports computational and cognitive modelling across courses but not a nine-credit dedicated theoretical-modelling component.
Both critically examine ethical and societal consequences of AI, including responsibility, fairness and human agency.
Both consider how systems or messages work for people; UCR focuses on evidence-based persuasive communication rather than product design.
Both develop personal, academic and professional formation in the first year.
UCR develops academic skills across its curriculum and PPD, but has no separate five-credit AI-specific academic-skills course.
UCR develops research and communication across several courses but not as a dedicated AI design-and-communication component.
UCR includes AI ethics and philosophy of mind but no dedicated philosophy-of-science-for-AI course.
UCR requires first-year PPD but has no separate second-year PPD continuation.
UCR AI Ethics examines fairness and bias, but no single course reproduces this dedicated intersectional-theory elective.
UCR AI Ethics and health courses provide related perspectives but no dedicated AI-ethics-in-healthcare component.
The comparator preserves 24 EC of genuine free choice.

notes.text: Radboud's Artificial Intelligence bachelor provides a tightly integrated 180-EC sequence across computer science, mathematics, statistics, cognitive science, neuroscience, psychology, linguistics, robotics, philosophy and a 12-EC thesis. UCR can assemble strong interdisciplinary AI pathways with substantial programming, algorithms, data, machine learning, robotics, cognition, ethics and research, but it does not reproduce the same continuous specialist sequence or dedicated components in natural-language processing, Bayesian methods, brain-computer interfacing and theoretical cognitive modelling.
